national_posture.statement: The latest available United States product was the August 5 IMSR at National Preparedness Level 5; it listed 94 uncontained large fires, 133 active incidents, and 28,700 assigned personnel, and remained current on the NIFC page at the August 6 cutoff.
national_posture.level_meaning: national resources are fully committed, active geographic areas may need emergency measures, and potential for additional significant fires is high

national_posture.statement: CWFIS statistics valid August 6 listed 674 active fires, 4,529 fires year to date, and 9,538,248 acres (3,859,788 hectares) burned year to date; the latest CIFFC report, issued August 5 at 4:20 PM EDT, placed Canada at National Preparedness Level 5 and British Columbia at agency preparedness level 5 with extreme national resource demand and international resources mobilizing.
national_posture.level_meaning: national demand is extreme, Canadian resources are fully committed, and international resources are being mobilized to sustain operations

incidents.name: Old Trails Fire
incidents.location: West of Spokane near Airway Heights

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect around the fire.

incidents.operational_outlook: Crews continued structure protection, perimeter control, damage assessment, and mop-up while hot and dry conditions sustained interior heat.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage combines the arson case and personal-loss stories with firefighters' 16-hour shifts, extensive displacement, drone incursions, and efforts to hold recent containment gains.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 47 items from 32 title-attributed publishers versus 98 in seven days, a 14.0-item daily baseline and 3.4-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

conflicting_values: The latest highlighted incident update reported Old Trails at 13% containment while current basic-information text elsewhere on the same page showed 5%; the newer highlighted update controls.
Current basic information sums individual Spokane fire areas to 10436 acres while the highlighted update and NBC reported 10546 total acres.
incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The newer highlighted official update and contemporaneous coverage support 13% containment; the current individual 3,574-acre basic-information field is retained for area while the conflicting complex-wide totals are disclosed. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-spokane-area-fires); [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/firefighters-are-working-16-hour-shifts-battle-spokane-complex-fire-rcna591062)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The IMSR's 570 losses are unspecified structures and must not be converted into dwellings. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Grasshopper Fire
incidents.location: Mt. Hood National Forest near Highway 35
incidents.controlling_agency: Mt. Hood National Forest and Oregon State Fire Marshal

evacuation.description: Level 3 Go Now orders remained in parts of Hood River and Wasco counties while Clackamas County maintained Level 1 Ready notices.

incidents.operational_outlook: Structural triage and preparation continued around Mt. Hood Meadows and Highway 35 while hot dry weather and gusty winds challenged control work.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage focuses on the fire's approach to Mount Hood landmarks, Level 3 evacuation areas around Mt. Hood Meadows, a Level 1 notice at Timberline Lodge, and the absence of confirmed structure loss.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 44 items from 22 title-attributed publishers versus 99 in seven days, a 14.1-item daily baseline and 3.1-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Official sources describe active structural triage and evacuation areas but do not report a destroyed-structure count; threat must remain qualitative. ([Oregon State Fire Marshal](https://apps.oregon.gov/oregon-newsroom/OR/OSFM/Posts/Post/grasshopper-805))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Bradley Creek Fire
incidents.location: Okanagan Indian Band reserve near Vernon

evacuation.description: Four evacuation orders and three alerts remained mapped around the Okanagan Indian Band and neighboring jurisdictions.

incidents.operational_outlook: BC Wildfire Service continued to classify the incident as out of control; current coverage emphasized continued response support for displaced residents.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage continues to center on the preliminary estimate of about 230 homes destroyed in the Okanagan Indian Band community while adding practical reporting on support for evacuees and changing B.C. fire conditions.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 40 items from 24 title-attributed publishers versus 87 in seven days, a 12.4-item daily baseline and 3.2-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The roughly 230-home estimate remains preliminary and was reported by the Okanagan Indian Band chief; it is not a completed parcel-level assessment. ([Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/wildfire-canada-homes-destroyed-british-columbia-fbbb7f027adb04a9c9b47a109de74082))
critical_alert_reasons: at least 25 newly damaged or destroyed structures
named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Autumn Lane Fire
incidents.location: Spokane and Stevens counties near Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and trail closures remained in effect around Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls.

incidents.operational_outlook: Fire managers continued aggressive wildland-urban-interface structure protection as poor overnight humidity recovery and critically dry fuels supported continued activity.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes crews holding fire lines, persistent evacuation constraints, long shifts, and the need to protect residences around Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 38 items from 25 title-attributed publishers versus 98 in seven days, a 14.0-item daily baseline and 2.7-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 80 losses are an unspecified-structure total while the continuing threat is residential; keep realized loss and residential exposure separate. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Rowe Creek Complex
incidents.location: South of Fossil across central Oregon counties
incidents.controlling_agency: Southwest Complex Incident Management Team 2 and Oregon State Fire Marshal

evacuation.description: The incident page directed residents to county maps and retained evacuation updates including Level 3 zones; no single complex-wide level applied.

incidents.operational_outlook: Crews strengthened containment and prepared private residences and outbuildings while a hot dry and unstable warning covered August 6.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes the complex's exceptional size and 62% containment while official basic information advanced to 340,276 acres after earlier reports cited about 329,000 acres.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 28 items from 20 title-attributed publishers versus 94 in seven days, a 13.4-item daily baseline and 2.1-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** Current InciWeb basic information showed 340,276 acres and 62% containment, superseding the August 5 IMSR's 325,265 acres and 57%; recent news captured intermediate values. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/orprd-rowe-creek-complex); [NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The complex-wide 25-loss total is not classified by occupancy.
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Fairview Fire

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect near Mead.

incidents.operational_outlook: Crews continued structure protection, perimeter control, systematic life-safety searches, and damage assessment around burned properties.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage treats Fairview as part of the wider Spokane disaster, emphasizing exhausting shifts, extensive displacement, and structure-loss assessment rather than a new Fairview-specific loss increment.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 24 items from 18 title-attributed publishers versus 81 in seven days, an 11.6-item daily baseline and 2.1-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

conflicting_values: The latest highlighted incident update reported Fairview at 5% containment while current basic-information text elsewhere on the same page showed 13%; the newer highlighted update controls.
incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 57 losses are unspecified structures and must not be converted into residences. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Widemouth 2 Fire
incidents.location: Fishlake National Forest between Kanosh, Meadow, and Fillmore
incidents.controlling_agency: Great Basin Complex Incident Management Team 2 and Fishlake National Forest

evacuation.description: Official incident information described evacuations from Meadow toward Fillmore and directed residents to county sheriffs for changing evacuation levels.

incidents.operational_outlook: Hot dry windy conditions and rapid spread continued to drive structure-protection work from Kanosh through Meadow toward Fillmore.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage says many residents were allowed home but warned to remain ready to leave again, while some locations remained under evacuation orders and the fire stayed active at zero containment.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 21 items from 14 title-attributed publishers versus 95 in seven days, a 13.6-item daily baseline and 1.5-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** News reports attributed a small damage count to local officials, but no reviewed controlling-agency source quantified damage by cutoff; structure loss therefore remains not reported in operational evidence. ([Utah Fire Info](https://www.facebook.com/UtahWildfire/posts/update-for-widemouth2fire-august-5-2026-800aminformation-line-435-261-3607curren/1595214785498719/))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Aspen Acres Fire

evacuation.description: Area and road closures remained in effect; the latest pre-cutoff update did not report an active evacuation count.

incidents.operational_outlook: A local Type 3 team assumed command as personnel declined and crews continued hot-spot work and repair under hot dry conditions.

attention.coverage_summary: Recent coverage emphasizes stable acreage and containment near 71%, the transition to a local team, declining personnel, and recovery work rather than a new loss increment.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 19 items from nine title-attributed publishers versus 82 in seven days, an 11.7-item daily baseline and 1.6-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cutoff note:** An August 6 InciWeb update appeared minutes after the 9:03 AM cutoff and was not used; the latest pre-cutoff official values remain 101,961 acres and 71%. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/copsf-aspen-acres-fire)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Treat the IMSR's 915 lost structures as cumulative and unspecified by occupancy. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))

incidents.name: Kaiser Canyon Fire
incidents.controlling_agency: Bureau of Indian Affairs and Alaska Incident Management Team 2

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and area closures remained in effect south of Nespelem.

incidents.operational_outlook: Fire remained active in hot dry conditions; crews continued structure protection along Highway 155 and the Highway 21 corridor.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes Kaiser Canyon's position as Washington's largest active fire, continuing structure protection, and the heat and wind threatening recent progress.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 18 items from 12 title-attributed publishers versus 54 in seven days, a 7.7-item daily baseline and 2.3-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** Current InciWeb basic information showed 136,887 acres and 43% containment, superseding the page's older August 5 daily update and IMSR values of 136,713 acres and 48%. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wacoa-kaiser-canyon); [NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 44 losses remain cumulative and unspecified by occupancy.
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Pear Lake Fire
incidents.location: Thompson-Nicola Regional District and Village of Clinton

evacuation.description: Eight evacuation orders and four alerts remained mapped from regional districts First Nations and the Village of Clinton.

incidents.operational_outlook: The fire remained out of control; current coverage described extreme behavior on the northwest flank and the arrival of Mexican reinforcements.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage combines incomplete property-loss assessment with renewed operational concern over extreme behavior on the northwest flank and incoming Mexican firefighting reinforcements.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible 24-hour query returned 14 items from 12 title-attributed publishers versus 61 in seven days, an 8.7-item daily baseline and 1.6-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Do not equate about 120 affected properties with destroyed dwellings; reported impacts include garages, sheds, and outbuildings, and assessment remained incomplete. ([CTV News](https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/more-than-100-structures-lost-in-bcs-pear-lake-wildfire-officials-say/))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

global_overview.statement: The reviewed international headline sample remained concentrated in Europe: fires around Greece drove the clearest current life-safety signal, France and Spain reported partial containment and returns alongside continuing alerts, and Albania still had active fires. No event in the reviewed Australia, Africa, Asia, or South America sample reached comparable headline and structural-impact prominence. This is a headline scan, not comprehensive worldwide operational intelligence.

global_events.name: Crete and southern Greece fires
global_events.status: Major fires remained active under high wind and heat, with Greece maintaining very high fire danger
global_events.evacuations: Hundreds of residents and tourists were evacuated by land and sea around Crete communities.
global_events.summary: Three firefighters were reported killed across Crete and the Peloponnese; reviewed sources did not provide a defensible structure-loss total.

global_events.name: Bordeaux–Le Porge fire
global_events.status: The fire was contained without overnight spread but not fully extinguished
global_events.evacuations: About 220,000 people evacuated during the event, with tens of thousands beginning to return.
global_events.summary: Access and recovery continued after the large evacuation while hot-weather alerts remained in force.

global_events.name: Central Spain and Almería fire complexes
global_events.status: The Madrid–Castilla y León fire had no active fronts and was downgraded, but other fires and heat kept Spain on alert
global_events.evacuations: About 1,000 residents remained evacuated near the San Juan reservoir; more than 1,500 had evacuated during the Almería fire.
global_events.summary: No consolidated national structure-loss total was available; prior reporting described losses among campsite mobile homes.

global_events.name: Mallakastër and Gjirokastër fires
global_events.status: Ground and aerial crews were protecting homes in Mallakastër while a second fire remained active south of Gjirokastër
global_events.evacuations: About 15 families were evacuated with livestock and pets.
global_events.summary: No verified structure-loss or burned-area count was published in the reviewed report.
